question.text: The potential energy function (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math> ) of a particle in a region of space is given as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>U</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>z</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>. Here <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>y</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi></math> are in meter. The magnitude of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> - component of force (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> ) acting on the particle at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is:

solution.text:
Given U=2x2+3y3+2z

The expression for the x-component of the force can be calculated as follows: 

Fx=-∂U∂x=-4x

Hence, at the point 1, 2, 3 m, the value of the force is given by

Fx=-4×1 N=4 N
